name: Thompson Dallas
positioning: Design-led Thompson hotel in The National, the restored 1960s First National Bank Tower in downtown Dallas
best_for: Travelers who want a downtown Dallas base with several restaurants and a rooftop pool in the building
Guests who want a spa with saunas and plunge pools on a terrace overlooking downtown

facts.text: The hotel is in the former First National Bank Tower, which has anchored Dallas's Main Street District since 1965.
The building's exterior was designed in the 1960s by architect George Dahl.
Thompson Dallas was the first Thompson hotel in Texas and takes up about half the building, with offices and residences on the upper floors.
Original materials such as the ninth floor's travertine walls were restored.
Rooms are designed with mid-century flair, walnut woods and brass touches.
Room decor brings in 1960s-style furniture, light fixtures and brass accents, styled with cow print and leather.
Rooms stock D.S. & Durga bath products.
Monarch, on the 49th floor, is a wood-fired modern Italian restaurant.
Monarch was imagined by chef Danny Grant and team.
Little Daisy is a Franco-American bistro.
The rooftop pool is on the ninth floor.
The rooftop pool has private cabanas with TVs to rent.

highlights.text: The National was once the tallest building west of the Mississippi.
The spa terrace overlooking downtown has infrared saunas and hot and cold plunge pools.
Catbird is a restaurant and lounge with a rooftop terrace overlooking downtown Dallas.
The hotel has some two acres of outdoor space.
The National also houses Samuel Lynne Galleries, showing contemporary art, and Lucchese, known for handcrafted Western style.

considerations.text: A daily destination fee, subject to change, applies to each room.
Conde Nast Traveler advises having a rental car to explore beyond a four-block radius.
The DART light rail can sometimes be faintly heard from the station below.
